name: date_arithmetic
title: Relative date arithmetic and comparisons
summary: Wrap python-dateutil to perform exact calendar arithmetic, weekday calculations, date differences, Easter dates, and free-form date parsing.

tools.name: adjust_date
tools.description: Add or subtract years, months, days, or weeks from a date using exact calendar arithmetic, including month-end clamping. Can also move to the nth occurrence of a weekday on or after the resulting date.

params.name: base_date
params.description: Starting date, preferably YYYY-MM-DD; any string parseable by dateutil.parser.parse is also accepted.

params.name: years
params.description: Years to add; negative values subtract.

params.name: months
params.description: Months to add; negative values subtract.

params.name: days
params.description: Days to add; negative values subtract.

params.name: weeks
params.description: Weeks to add; negative values subtract.

params.name: weekday
params.description: Optional weekday name to advance to: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, or Sunday.

params.name: weekday_occurrence
params.description: Which occurrence of weekday to use when weekday is provided. Defaults to 1.

returns.name: days_applied
returns.description: Days component applied, including weeks converted to days by the library.

returns.name: weekday_applied
returns.description: Weekday applied, or an empty string when none.

returns.name: weekday_occurrence_applied
returns.description: Weekday occurrence applied, or 0 when none.

tools.implementation_notes: Import relativedelta and weekday constants from dateutil.relativedelta, and parse from dateutil.parser. Convert base_date with parse(base_date).date(). Map weekday names to MO, TU, WE, TH, FR, SA, and SU; if weekday is provided, construct the weekday value as weekday_constant(weekday_occurrence or 1). Call relativedelta(years=years, months=months, days=days, weeks=weeks, weekday=weekday_value) and add it to the parsed date. Return result.isoformat() and result.strftime('%A'). If no weekday is supplied, pass weekday=None.

tools.name: date_difference
tools.description: Compute the exact difference between two dates in years, months, and days, plus the total number of days.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Earlier or reference date, preferably YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: end_date
params.description: Later or target date, preferably YYYY-MM-DD.

returns.name: start_date
returns.description: Normalized start date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: end_date
returns.description: Normalized end date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

returns.name: months
returns.description: Difference in months after removing whole years.

returns.name: days
returns.description: Difference in days after removing whole months.

tools.implementation_notes: Import relativedelta from dateutil.relativedelta and parse from dateutil.parser. Convert both inputs with parse(...).date(), then call relativedelta(end_date, start_date). Return rd.years, rd.months, and rd.days. Compute total_days as (end_date - start_date).days using standard date subtraction.

tools.name: easter_date
tools.description: Return the date of Easter for a given year using the Western, Orthodox, or Julian calendar.

params.name: year
params.description: Calendar year for which to compute Easter.

params.name: method
params.description: Easter calendar method: western, orthodox, or julian. Defaults to western.

returns.name: weekday
returns.description: Weekday name of the Easter date.

tools.implementation_notes: Import easter and the EASTER_WESTERN, EASTER_ORTHODOX, and EASTER_JULIAN constants from dateutil.easter. Map the method string to the corresponding constant, defaulting to EASTER_WESTERN, then call easter(year, method=constant). Return the resulting date's isoformat() and strftime('%A'). Raise a ValueError for an unrecognized method string.

tools.name: parse_date
tools.description: Parse a free-form date or datetime string and return it in ISO format with related calendar fields.

params.name: text
params.description: Date or datetime string in a free-form or standard format.

returns.name: iso_datetime
returns.description: Parsed value in ISO 8601 format, including time when present.

returns.name: weekday
returns.description: Weekday name of the parsed date.

returns.name: day_of_year
returns.description: Day number within the parsed year.

tools.implementation_notes: Import parse from dateutil.parser. Call parse(text), then return dt.date().isoformat() for iso_date, dt.isoformat() for iso_datetime, dt.year, dt.month, dt.day, dt.strftime('%A'), and dt.timetuple().tm_yday. Parsing errors from the library propagate as ValueError.

excluded_symbols.reason: Not needed for the requested date arithmetic and comparison operations.
Scaling relativedeltas is outside the requested capability.

side_effects: None; all operations are pure computations.
Invalid date strings or unsupported Easter methods propagate library exceptions, typically ValueError.
uncertainties: Month-end clamping behavior is delegated to dateutil.relativedelta and follows its documented rules.
weekday_occurrence is not strictly validated; values outside the usual 1-5 range may move the result beyond the original month.
Free-form date parsing depends on dateutil.parser.parse and may interpret ambiguous strings according to its default rules.
Easter methods are mapped to dateutil constants; unsupported method strings are rejected before calling the library.
Date inputs are ultimately constrained by Python's supported date range.
